text:
cheng: Pushed a small KV-cache microbenchmark across GPUs and regions — results + artifacts: https://drive.redwood.ai/kv-bench-1769 (charts + raw csv). TL;DR: paging-induced p99 tail varies a lot by GPU and region; eviction policy matters more for heavy long-tail seqs.

maya: Nice, can you summarize the key numbers?

cheng: Sure. High-level numbers (single-GPU, 128B context, 2000 qps emulated, cache capacity 6GB keys):
- A100 (us-west): hitrate 78%, p50 12ms, p95 28ms, p99 48ms
- A100 (eu-west): hitrate 75%, p50 14ms, p95 36ms, p99 96ms  <-- big tail, likely PCIe host->GPU variance
- H100 (us-west): hitrate 79%, p50 10ms, p95 22ms, p99 34ms
- L40 (us-west): hitrate 72%, p50 18ms, p95 40ms, p99 82ms

Also tested eviction: LRU vs segmented-LRU (SLRU) vs FIFO. SLRU gave ~+4% hitrate on 256+ seq mixes and reduced p99 by ~18% vs LRU for those mixes. FIFO performed worst on skewed access.

liam: Were you running the same kernel set across GPUs (flash vs fused) and same batching?

cheng: Yes — batching controlled at request layer (batch sizes tried: 1,4,8). Kernel choice was auto-selected by our runtime but we forced comparisons. Observations:
- For seq <= 64, flash-attention kernels had lower p50/p95 across all GPUs.
- For seq > 128, our partitioned/fused kernels (memory-friendly) had better stability and lower p99 on H100.
- For A100 in eu-west, using fused kernels + SLRU reduced p99 by ~22% compared to default mapping (runtime auto).

anika: For Dedicated customers, what's the capacity guidance? How many GPUs per 1k sustained qps for mixed seq distribution?

cheng: For a production mix we observed (seq dist: 16: 40%, 64: 35%, 256+: 25%) — with SLRU + tuned kernel mapping:~
- H100: ~5 GPUs per 1k qps (95th latency SLO 50ms)
- A100: ~7 GPUs per 1k qps (95th latency SLO 60ms), but region variability can push more margin
- L40: ~8-9 GPUs per 1k qps, higher for heavy 256+ mixes
These are approximate; see the "capacity_sizing.md" artifact in the drive link.

oliver: Can you drop the raw csv here? I want to run our analyzer.

cheng: uploaded raw CSVs + notebook: https://drive.redwood.ai/kv-bench-1769/raw.zip. The notebook has the plotting code and the exact Triton kernel mapping used. Example harness command we ran:

```
./kv_bench --model gpt-like --gpu-type H100 --region us-west --seq-dist "16:40,64:35,256:25" --qps 2000 --cache-size-mb 6144 --eviction slru --batching "1,4,8"
```

maya: Any surprising failure modes?

cheng: Two gotchas: 1) PCIe host saturation in eu region during heavy page-in spikes — we saw OS-level stalls that inflated p99; adding a prefetcher reduced those spikes but increased avg bandwidth. 2) Kernel selection heuristics in runtime occasionally pick flash for mid sequences (80-140) which raises tail on A100; adding a heuristics override helps.

perf-bot: perf-bot has logged a regression alert: eu-west A100 p99 increased by 37% vs last run (tag: kv-cache/2026-03-18).

anika: Let's add a follow-up item: run same bench on ap-southeast (L40 availability) and retest with prefetcher toggles. Marking as action item.

oliver: I'll add a quick dashboard tile for p99 by region + kernel mapping.

cheng: Cool. I'll open a short RFC with config suggestions and include a small canary to flip kernel mapping for A100 eu-west. Link when ready. :thumbsup:
